sources.title: A. Jaffe, E. Witten, Quantum Yang–Mills Theory (official problem description)
Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules (adopted 2018-09-26)
R. F. Streater, A. S. Wightman, PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That (1964) — reference [45] of S1
K. Osterwalder, R. Schrader, CMP 31 (1973) 83–112 and CMP 42 (1975) 281–305 — reference [35] of S1

requirements.title: Target object
requirements.text: For each admissible $G$ a quantum field theory $\mathcal T_G=(\mathcal H,U,\Omega,\mathcal D,\{\mathcal O_i\}_{i\in I})$ on Minkowski space $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:wightman}.

requirements.title: All gauge groups
requirements.text: The statement holds for \emph{every} compact simple gauge group. Constants (including $\Delta$) may depend on $G$; uniformity in $G$ is \emph{not} required.

requirements.title: Space-time $\mathbb R^4$
requirements.text: The theory lives on $\mathbb R^4$: not on a lattice, not on a torus $T^4$, not in dimension $d<4$, and without any remaining UV or IR cut-off.

requirements.title: Non-triviality
requirements.text: $\mathcal T_G$ is non-trivial. The term is not defined in S1; working definition in \ref{I-1}.

requirements.title: Hilbert space and symmetry
requirements.text: A separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ with a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of the restricted Poincar\'e group $\mathcal P_+^\uparrow$ (or its covering group).

requirements.title: Spectrum condition
requirements.text: The joint spectrum of the generators $(H,\vec P)$ lies in the closed forward cone $\overline V_+$; in particular $H\ge 0$.

requirements.title: Vacuum
requirements.text: A Poincar\'e-invariant vector $\Omega\in\mathcal H$, unique up to a phase.

requirements.title: Local fields
requirements.text: Operator-valued tempered distributions $\mathcal O_i$ on a common dense $U$-invariant domain $\mathcal D\ni\Omega$, Poincar\'e-covariant, with $\Omega$ cyclic for the polynomial field algebra.

requirements.title: Locality
requirements.text: $[\mathcal O_i(f),\mathcal O_j(g)]=0$ on $\mathcal D$ whenever $\operatorname{supp}f$ and $\operatorname{supp}g$ are space-like separated.

requirements.title: Field content
requirements.text: Local fields correspond to gauge-invariant local polynomials in $F$ and its covariant derivatives (e.g.\ $\operatorname{Tr}F_{ij}F_{kl}$). The correspondence is dimension-filtered, not a naive bijection.

requirements.title: Short-distance identity
requirements.text: Correlation functions agree at short distances with asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization theory.

requirements.title: Stress tensor and OPE
requirements.text: Existence of a stress tensor and of an operator product expansion with the local singularities predicted by asymptotic freedom.

requirements.title: Mass gap
requirements.text: $\exists\,\Delta>0:\ \sigma(H)\cap(0,\Delta)=\varnothing$.

requirements.title: Finite mass
requirements.text: $m:=\sup\{\Delta\}<\infty$. Equivalently $H\neq 0$; with \ref{A-027} this excludes exactly $\mathcal H=\mathbb C\Omega$.

requirements.title: Axiomatic strength
requirements.text: Axiomatic properties at least as strong as S3 and S4. On the Euclidean route: the OS axioms in the corrected form of [OS75], including the linear growth condition (\ref{A-001}, \ref{A-002}).

requirements.title: No weak existence
requirements.text: Existence by compactness (subsequential limits) alone is excluded unless the axioms and the mass gap are established for the limit.

requirements.title: UV regulator removed
requirements.text: Every UV regulator (lattice spacing $a$, momentum cut-off, \dots) is removed; the topology of convergence of the correlation functions is specified.

requirements.title: IR regulator removed
requirements.text: Every IR regulator (volume $L$, boundary conditions) is removed; dependence on boundary conditions is absent or controlled.

requirements.title: Properties survive limits
requirements.text: Reflection positivity, full Euclidean invariance $E(4)$ (restored from any lattice subgroup), locality, gauge invariance of observables and the gap bound hold for the \emph{limit}, not only along the approximation.

requirements.title: Complete proof
requirements.text: A complete mathematical solution: every step is proved, or reduced to a published theorem whose hypotheses are verified in the instance.

requirements.title: Explicit correspondence
requirements.text: The paper addresses the specific questions of the official description; a closely related question does not qualify.

requirements.title: Self-containment
requirements.text: CMI does not consider supplementary material submitted by the author: every essential step must be in the published work.

requirements.title: Qualifying Outlet
requirements.text: Publication in a refereed mathematics publication of worldwide repute with named editorial board, qualified editors, a published refereeing process and MathSciNet listing. CMI keeps no list and gives no advice.

requirements.title: Time and acceptance
requirements.text: At least two years since publication, survival of rigorous examination and general acceptance in the global mathematics community; only then may CMI decide on detailed consideration by a special advisory committee.

requirements.title: Priority record
requirements.text: CMI pays special attention to dependence on prior published insights: keep a contribution and priority ledger from day one.

interpretations.title: Non-triviality
interpretations.issue: S1 requires a \enquote{non-trivial} theory but does not define the term.
interpretations.reading: $\mathcal T_G$ is not isomorphic to (i) the one-dimensional theory $\mathcal H=\mathbb C\Omega$ (already excluded by YM-14), (ii) the Wick-polynomial theory of $\dim\mathfrak g$ free massless vector fields (already excluded by YM-13, since it is gapless), or (iii) a generalized free (Gaussian) theory. Recommended certificate: prove YM-11 for at least one connected $n$-point function, $n\ge 3$, whose leading perturbative coefficient is non-zero.
interpretations.positive: The certificate settles YM-04 and part of YM-11 together.
interpretations.negative: A result of the form \enquote{only trivial theories exist} must exclude (iii) explicitly.

interpretations.title: Compact simple gauge group
interpretations.issue: As an abstract group $SU(N)$ is not simple (centre $\mathbb Z_N$). The physics usage is: compact connected Lie group with simple, non-abelian Lie algebra. Different global forms (e.g.\ $SU(N)$ and $SU(N)/\mathbb Z_N$) share the local operator content on $\mathbb R^4$ and differ in line operators and $\theta$-periodicity [AST13].
interpretations.reading: The quantifier ranges over all compact simple Lie algebras $\mathfrak g\in\{A_n(n\ge1),B_n(n\ge2),C_n(n\ge3),D_n(n\ge4),E_6,E_7,E_8,F_4,G_2\}$, each with any compact connected $G$ such that $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\mathfrak g$.
interpretations.positive: A method that works only for $SU(3)$, or only for $SU(N)$, does not suffice: all four classical families and all five exceptional algebras are required.
interpretations.negative: A counterexample for one single $\mathfrak g$ suffices.

interpretations.title: Theta parameter
interpretations.issue: The Lagrangian (1) of S1 has no topological $\theta$-term, although the quantum theory admits one.
interpretations.negative: Unless CMI's reading restricts to $\theta=0$, a non-existence result would also have to cover $\theta\neq0$. Flag for expert confirmation.

interpretations.title: Short-distance agreement
interpretations.issue: \enquote{Agree at short distances with the predictions of asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization theory, as described in textbooks} does not specify which correlation functions or to which order.
interpretations.reading: For gauge-invariant local fields, Schwinger functions at non-coinciding points, scaled towards a point, have asymptotic expansions in the running coupling $\bar g(\mu)$ that match renormalized perturbation theory order by order. Minimal certificate: leading-logarithmic agreement including the universal coefficients $b_0,b_1$ (\ref{A-009}).
interpretations.positive: The order of agreement must be stated explicitly in the main theorem.
interpretations.negative: Ambiguity here is a candidate for S2 \S5(c)(ii) (reformulation), not for the Prize.

interpretations.title: Axiom set
interpretations.issue: \enquote{At least as strong as those cited in [45, 35]}: [45] gives the Wightman axioms, [35] is OS~I \emph{and} OS~II. The reconstruction claim of OS~I is false without the linear growth condition (\ref{A-002}).
interpretations.reading: Wightman axioms as in Definition~\ref{def:wightman}; on the Euclidean route the OS axioms including the linear growth condition of [OS75]. A Haag--Kastler net alone is not sufficient, because the requirement cites [45, 35], not [24].
interpretations.positive: Prove OS0$'$ (linear growth) explicitly; it is the axiom most often forgotten.
interpretations.negative: \enquote{The axioms are too restrictive} is an opinion, not a counterexample (Section~\ref{sec:negative}).

interpretations.title: Form of publication
interpretations.issue: S2 speaks of \enquote{the Proposed Solution} published in a Qualifying Outlet and does not say how a series of papers is treated.
interpretations.reading: A series of refereed papers is acceptable in principle, but one main paper must contain the complete logical chain (the \enquote{Clay corollary}) with exact references to the published components.
interpretations.positive: No essential step may live only in code, data or supplements (YM-22).

assumptions.text: OS reconstruction: Schwinger functions satisfying OS0$'$ (linear growth) and OS1--OS3 define a Wightman theory; cluster (OS4) $\Leftrightarrow$ uniqueness of the vacuum.
assumptions.scope: Exact theorem numbers to be pinned before use.

assumptions.text: \enquote{OS axioms without the linear growth condition suffice for reconstruction} (claim of OS~I).
assumptions.scope: Proof error (Lemma 8.8 of OS~I); corrected in OS~II by adding the linear growth condition. Precedent: a foundational claim was falsified and repaired in print.

assumptions.text: The Wilson lattice gauge theory with compact $G$ is reflection positive.
assumptions.scope: Wilson action; lattice reflections.

assumptions.text: Lattice Yang--Mills at strong coupling (small $\beta$) has exponential clustering (a lattice mass gap) and an area law.
assumptions.scope: Only $\beta<\beta_0(G,d)$. The continuum limit requires $\beta\to\infty$ (weak coupling): the opposite regime.

assumptions.text: Renormalization-group control of the 4D lattice gauge theory on a torus, uniformly in the lattice spacing (ultraviolet stability).
assumptions.scope: Fixed finite volume. Expectations of gauge-invariant observables and the continuum limit are not completed (S1 \S6.5).

assumptions.text: Construction of YM$_4$ with an infrared cut-off in a continuum regularization.
assumptions.scope: IR cut-off remains; reflection positivity is not automatic for continuum regularizations (S1 \S6.5).

assumptions.text: \enquote{A global continuous gauge-fixing section exists on the space of connections.}
assumptions.scope: Gribov ambiguity; Singer's theorem. Gauge fixing is only local or patchwise. A failing gauge-fixing method is not a counterexample to S1.

assumptions.text: The formal path integral $Z^{-1}e^{-S_{\mathrm{YM}}(A)}\prod_x dA(x)$ is a measure.
assumptions.scope: No such measure is known; guidance only.

assumptions.text: $\beta(g)=-b_0g^3-b_1g^5+O(g^7)$ with $b_0=\tfrac{11}{3}\tfrac{C_A}{16\pi^2}$, $b_1=\tfrac{34}{3}\tfrac{C_A^2}{(16\pi^2)^2}$, $C_A=h^\vee(\mathfrak g)>0$ for every simple $\mathfrak g$.
assumptions.scope: Perturbative statement. Its non-perturbative meaning must be proved (YM-11).

assumptions.text: \enquote{The perturbation series in $g$ converges.}
assumptions.scope: Divergent in most known examples; Borel methods of limited use.

assumptions.text: Lattice Monte Carlo: lightest $0^{++}$ glueball of $SU(3)$ at about $1.7$~GeV ($1730(50)(80)$ and $1710(50)(80)$ MeV).
assumptions.scope: Evidence, never proof. Use: sanity check for any claimed rigorous bound.

assumptions.text: \enquote{$\Delta_{a,L}>0$ for all $(a,L)$ implies a positive gap in the limit.}
assumptions.scope: Non-uniform bounds may tend to $0$. A uniform bound in physical units is required (\ref{A-031}).

assumptions.text: \enquote{A subsequential (compactness) limit settles existence.}
assumptions.scope: Explicitly excluded unless the axioms and the gap are proved for the limit (YM-16).

assumptions.text: Scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and lattice $\phi^4$ models are Gaussian (marginal triviality).
assumptions.scope: Calibration: a rigorous 4D negative result concerns a specified class of approximations. The published proof itself received a corrigendum (2024).

assumptions.text: Self-interacting single-component $\phi^4$ fields do not exist in $d\ge5$.
assumptions.scope: Calibration for the negative track. Yang--Mills differs: it is asymptotically free.

assumptions.text: Under YM-05--YM-09 with a unique vacuum: gap of $H$ $\Leftrightarrow$ gap of $M=\sqrt{H^2-\vec P^2}$ on $\Omega^\perp$ $\Leftrightarrow$ uniform exponential decay in Euclidean time of truncated two-point functions of a vacuum-cyclic field family.
assumptions.scope: Locators to be pinned. Main tool for proving YM-13 from Euclidean data.

assumptions.text: Gap $\Rightarrow$ clustering: for every $C<\Delta$ and every local $\mathcal O$ with $\langle\Omega,\mathcal O\Omega\rangle=0$, $|\langle\Omega,\mathcal O(\vec x)\mathcal O(\vec y)\Omega\rangle|\le e^{-C|\vec x-\vec y|}$ for large $|\vec x-\vec y|$.
assumptions.scope: Independent consistency check of any gap proof.

assumptions.text: Full Euclidean invariance $E(4)$ is restored in the continuum limit of the Wilson lattice theory, whose symmetry is only hypercubic.
assumptions.scope: Critical and easy to overlook.

assumptions.text: Renormalized gauge-invariant composite fields (e.g.\ $\operatorname{Tr}F^2$) arise as limits of lattice observables, with finite additive and multiplicative renormalization and mixing only with fields of lower or equal dimension.
assumptions.scope: Needed for YM-10 to YM-12.

assumptions.text: Reflection positivity is preserved under pointwise limits of Schwinger functionals on a fixed class of test functions.
assumptions.scope: Elementary (limits of positive semi-definite forms). The test-function classes along the approximation must match.

assumptions.text: The linear growth condition OS0$'$ holds uniformly along the approximation and passes to the limit.
assumptions.scope: Needed for A-001.

assumptions.text: Confinement (area law for Wilson loops).
assumptions.scope: \emph{Not} required by S1 (listed as an extension). Must not be used as a premise unless proved.

assumptions.text: Two-dimensional Yang--Mills on compact surfaces is constructed and exactly solvable.
assumptions.scope: No propagating gluons in 2D: a source of techniques, not evidence for the 4D gap.

assumptions.text: The 2D abelian Higgs model satisfies the OS axioms (BFS) and has a mass gap.
assumptions.scope: As of S1, the only complete interacting gauge theory satisfying the axioms.

assumptions.text: The gap may require a non-classical change of variables or duality transformation.
assumptions.scope: Research direction. Any duality used must itself be proved.

assumptions.text: Large-$N$ gauge/string duality for pure Yang--Mills.
assumptions.scope: S1: \enquote{no effective approach to the gauge theory without fermions}.

assumptions.text: In a Wightman theory with a unique vacuum, every translation-invariant vector is a multiple of $\Omega$.
assumptions.scope: Locator to be pinned. Used in YM-14 and A-016.

assumptions.text: Compact simple Lie algebras and dual Coxeter numbers: $h^\vee(A_n)=n+1$, $h^\vee(B_n)=2n-1$, $h^\vee(C_n)=n+1$, $h^\vee(D_n)=2n-2$, $h^\vee(E_6,E_7,E_8,F_4,G_2)=12,18,30,9,4$.
assumptions.scope: Normalization: long roots of length$^2=2$.

assumptions.text: Lean~4 formalization of the 4D free field satisfying the Glimm--Jaffe (OS-type) axioms.
assumptions.scope: Tooling precedent for Section~\ref{sec:verification}.

assumptions.text: Public Lean~4 formalization of OS reconstruction (third-party repository).
assumptions.scope: Not independently reviewed here. Candidate infrastructure only.

assumptions.text: Uniform gap: $\exists\,c>0,\ a_0>0,\ L_0<\infty$ such that $\Delta_{a,L}\ge c\,\Lambda$ for all $0<a<a_0$, $L>L_0$ (physical units, $\Lambda$ a renormalized scale).
assumptions.scope: S1: \enquote{New ideas are needed}. The core open problem.

assumptions.text: Non-triviality certificate of \ref{I-1}: a connected $n\ge3$ function of gauge-invariant fields matches its non-zero leading perturbative coefficient.
assumptions.scope: Needed for YM-04.

assumptions.text: The construction is uniform in method across all compact simple $\mathfrak g$ (or is carried out algebra by algebra).
assumptions.scope: Needed for YM-02. Constants may depend on $\mathfrak g$.

transitions.title: Regularized model
transitions.text: Wilson measure $\mu_{a,L}$ on $G^{\text{links}}$: finite-dimensional, gauge invariant, reflection positive.

transitions.title: UV limit $a\to0$ at fixed $L$
transitions.text: Existence of the continuum limit on $T^4$ for gauge-invariant observables.

transitions.title: IR limit $L\to\infty$
transitions.text: Infinite-volume limit on $\mathbb R^4$, driven by a volume-uniform gap or cluster bound.

transitions.title: Symmetry restoration
transitions.text: From hypercubic to full $E(4)$ invariance of the limiting Schwinger functions.

transitions.title: Euclidean $\to$ Minkowski
transitions.text: OS reconstruction of a Wightman theory with unique vacuum.

transitions.title: Field content and UV identity
transitions.text: Renormalized local gauge-invariant fields, asymptotic freedom, stress tensor and OPE.

transitions.title: Non-triviality
transitions.text: The limit is not trivial or Gaussian (\ref{I-1}).

transitions.title: Mass gap in the limit
transitions.text: Positive spectral gap of the reconstructed $H$; clustering (\ref{A-017}) as an independent check.

transitions.title: All gauge groups
transitions.text: T1--T8 for every compact simple $\mathfrak g$.
